---
title: "EIR, HBR, prevalence, and cases"
---




Four quantities move through the pipeline. Each is either a single number or a path
through time, and that is what decides which package produces it.

## The four quantities

The **entomological inoculation rate (EIR)** is infectious bites per person per year. It
sets the force of infection in the underlying model, and it is the quantity the emulator
runs from. `estimint` infers it from prevalence or from HBR.

The **human biting rate (HBR)** is bites per person per year, infectious or not. It is
the EIR divided by the sporozoite rate, so the numbers are large, typically in the tens
or hundreds of thousands per year. `mosquito_delta` acts through the HBR.

Prevalence is reported throughout MINTverse as the under-five value on a 0 to 1 scale. It
appears both as an input (`prev_y9`, a single number describing the setting at the
decision point) and as an output (a 157-step trajectory from the emulator).

Cases are clinical malaria episodes, all-age, per 1000 population, and an emulator output
only. Nothing in the pipeline takes cases as an input, and there is no cases-to-anything
inversion. They are floored at zero.

## Values and series

| Quantity | What it is | Units | Value or series | Produced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EIR | transmission intensity | infectious bites / person / year | single value | `estimint` |
| HBR | biting pressure | bites / person / year | single value | `estimint` |
| Prevalence | infected share, under-5 | proportion, 0–1 | input value **or** 157-step series | input; `stateMINT` |
| Cases | clinical episodes, all-age | per 1000 population | 157-step series | `stateMINT` |

`estimint` returns an equilibrium, the transmission intensity that a setting sustains at
the moment the decision is taken. It has no time axis and cannot acquire one. It cannot
say what the EIR will be two years after a PBO campaign, because the model does not
represent time at all.

Only `stateMINT` returns a path. A trajectory, a comparison of trajectories, or an
endline value three years out has to come from the emulator.

::: {.callout-note}
## EIR and equilibrium

`estimate_eir_with_mosquito_delta` returns two numbers, `eir_baseline` and `eir_new`.
Both are equilibria. `eir_new` is the intensity a setting would settle at with a
different mosquito density, not the EIR at some later date, and the two values do not
bracket a trajectory between them. Any transient between the two is the emulator's
business.
:::

## The year-9 framing

Every trajectory the emulator returns is laid on the same grid. The grid is built around
the campaign.

The simulations behind `stateMINT` run a six-year burn-in first, letting the
transmission model settle into equilibrium from arbitrary initial conditions. That
burn-in is **discarded**, and never reaches the emulator.

What remains starts at day 2190, the start of year 6, and runs in 14-day windows. The
first three years are pre-campaign baseline, during which nothing changes. At day 3285,
the start of year 9, the campaign switches on. `dn0_future`, `itn_future`, `irs_future`,
`lsm` and `routine` are zero for every step before that day, and take their value from it
onwards. Roughly three years of response follow.

The grid is written into the artefact rather than hard-coded, so it can be read back.

::: {#ce9afb67 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
from stateMINT.model import Mamba2Regressor

artifact = Mamba2Regressor.from_pretrained(
    "dide-ic/stateMINT", predictor="prevalence", revision="v1.2.2",
)
cfg = artifact.preprocessing_config

abs_t = cfg["model_start_day"] + cfg["window_size"] * np.arange(cfg["n_steps"])
years = (abs_t - cfg["intervention_day"]) / 365
idx_y9 = int(np.argmin(np.abs(abs_t - cfg["intervention_day"])))

print(f"steps                {cfg['n_steps']}")
print(f"window               {cfg['window_size']} days")
print(f"grid starts          day {abs_t[0]}")
print(f"campaign             day {cfg['intervention_day']} -> step {idx_y9} (day {abs_t[idx_y9]})")
print(f"grid ends            day {abs_t[-1]}")
print(f"years from campaign  {years[0]:+.2f} to {years[-1]:+.2f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
steps                157
window               14 days
grid starts          day 2190
campaign             day 3285 -> step 78 (day 3282)
grid ends            day 4374
years from campaign  -3.00 to +2.98
```
:::
:::


The name `prev_y9` is literal. It is the annual mean under-five prevalence in year 9, the
year the campaign lands. When you pass a measured prevalence to `estimint`, you are
asserting that this is the setting as it stands on the day the nets are distributed.

The three pre-campaign years also serve as a sanity check. No campaign acts on them, so
they show the setting under the nets it already has. A baseline that starts somewhere
other than the prevalence you supplied indicates that the covariates do not describe the
setting you think they do.

Plotting in `years` rather than raw days puts the campaign at zero, so scenarios line
up on one x-axis.
